title: solo building an production-scale mmo with astra (in 3 days)
author: kalin_r
selftext:
when astra dropped i started working on this project, a production-scale mmo to see where i could push the new model, turns out, it's insanely good

the goal was loosely wow-classic era tech + scale, and it reached that benchmark  
20k\~ players on server, 2k\~ players in the same small area (100kb/s client in, 40mb/s server out)

honestly i think thats a little ahead of where wow classic servers were on count + bandwidth, but computers are much faster now; though i think there's still room for optimization

im not an artist so obviously the art is very poor, but that's astra throwing stuff together with no concept reference, but it IS the correct animation and triangle budget, so it's a suitable performance test

now, it's important to note that all those players are running as proper players connected to the server through network sockets (seperate process runs 20k headless game clients, and network connects to the server); so this is a true bandwidth/network/server test, the server cannot differentiate these from true players. however, obviously each bot player does very simple logic here so my machine can run 20k of them

so yeah, astra is absolutely insane. unfortunately this used 2 resets and all my tokens so had to slow down after this, but it's a good model

[https://24.199.125.91/](https://24.199.125.91/)

i put up the test server here if anyone wants to mess around  
the gameplay is very basic still, but systems-wise it should all work

comments.author: Interesting-Yellow-4
comments.body: Still a long way to go, but kudos on taking on the challenge. This is not going to be easy.

replies.author: kalin_r
replies.body: all the fun stuff is not easy

comments.author: egonosz
comments.body: It seems like the connected clients have some net code issues, if they are connected locally headless, they should move properly, without lag. Is the game logic client or server authoritative?

replies.author: kalin_r
replies.body:
everything is running with simulated latency, packetloss and it's running in it's worst-case situation (2k clients very close); so it's pushing my machine pretty hard so server updates is a bit behind 30hz target

would have a little more overhead if i wasnt running 20 thousand (!) local headless clients

the entire thing is server authorative, but this is a view from a client running locally but still network connected through the same system

also it's only a few days first pass so there's more that could be done for movement interpolation improvements under heavy load, im sure if i just dropped it to 1000\~ players and ran it at local 1ms latency it would be fine, but that's not a useful benchmark

replies.author: egonosz
replies.body:
Sure it is not useful benchmark, but it would look way better for demonstration. But even then it looks kind of suspicious characters teleporting back multiple times. 

But cool stuff! 

By the way I guess it is extrapolation and movement prediction. If you want it to look less laggy, you can extrapolate with slowing velocity based on last package arrival time.

replies.author: kalin_r
replies.body:
yeah, i guess i just grabbed a quick video not trying to make a trailer you know lol

it's already improved since that build, but yeah it was just some poor movement prediction / logic; a little better now but i expect / intend some rubber banding like that at 2000\~ players on screen (to hit the 100kb/s\~ client rate); i could always up the bandwidth or half the players but you know

comments.author: namezam
comments.body: Did astra make the trees with textures it generated or is that simulated with polygons? I’m struggling to make my games look good without having to import external textures and even then it doesn’t map them right. So basically all assets are coming externally. I even bought a tripo sub and damn I feel ripped off, I can’t get anything to look good.

replies.author: kalin_r
replies.body:
yeah it used  blender mcp to build the tree mesh and it's imagegen for the textures, and some python tools for editing

i didnt spend too much time on editing tbh, i explained the tree structure to it and got those in but only really astra-high and xhigh can model well and i spent the tokens on engineering instead

i cant find a good solution too, meshy/tripo etc doesn't really work too well for me. i think you need a good reference image to model pipeline, but havent spent that much time on the art side; might have to have a dedicated pro sub that just runs modeling
